answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by binding each identity to a non-transferable compute stake that must be re-proven every epoch against unique local conditions. Think of it as extracting shale that only yields a pearl once the vine of continuous peer-attested history has grown. A farm cannot cheaply clone the stake: each head must independently re-mine its own shale-derived proof while graders verify the vine remains intact, so large-scale identity farming becomes uneconomical once the pearl of established standing is required for full rewards.
